For $a=1:$ L.H.L. $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left(\left[(1-h)^2\right]-[1-h]^2\right)=0\text{ R.H.L. }=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left(\left[(1+h)^2\right]-[1+h]^2\right)=1-1=0\therefore$ Limit exist for $a=1$
For $a=2$ : L.H.L. $=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left(\left[(2-h)^2\right]-[2-h]^2\right)=3-1=2\text{ R.H.L. }=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left(\left[(2+h)^2\right]-[2+h]^2\right)=4-4=0\therefore$ Limit doesn't exist for $a=2$
Hence, for 2 values of ' $a$ ' limit doesn't exist.

$⇒ f\left(f\left(x\right) \cdot f\left(y\right)\right) = f\left(yx\right) + y + f\left(x\right) . . . \left(3\right)$ {from equation $2$}

questions.solution:
Given, $f:[-2,2] \rightarrow R$
$$

$$

& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{-2 c h}{-h(1+1)}=c
\end{aligned}
$$
and
$$
\mathrm{RHL}=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} f(x)
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} f(0+h)=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{0+h+3}{0+h+1} \\
& =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0} \frac{h+3}{h+1}=\frac{0+3}{0+1}=3
\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.solution: $Given, \begin{aligned} f(x) & = \begin{cases}x-5 & \text{$ for $} x \leq 1 \\ 4 x^2-9 & \text{ for } 1 < x < 2 \\ 3 x+4 & \text{ for } x \geq 2\end{cases} \\ f^{\prime}\left(2^{+}\right) & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}}\left(\frac{f(x)-f(2)}{x-2}\right) \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} \frac{3 x+4-(6+4)}{x-2} \\ & =\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \frac{3 x-6}{x-2} \\ & =3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\lim _{x \rightarrow \pi / 6} \left[\frac{3 \sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x}{6 x-\pi}\right]$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{3 \sin x-\sqrt{3} \cos x}{6 x-\pi}$
Using L, Hospitals' rule,
$=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{6}} \frac{3 \cos x+\sqrt{3} \sin x}{6}=\frac{3 \cos \frac{\pi}{6}+\sqrt{3} \sin \frac{\pi}{6}}{6}=\frac{3 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{6}=\frac{\frac{4 \sqrt{3}}{2}}{6}=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}}{6}=\frac{1}{3} \sqrt{3}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
